name: App building
blurb: Native-feeling mobile and desktop apps: Expo, SwiftUI, Compose, Flutter, Tauri, simulator checks, TestFlight and Play releases.
searches: Expo SDK release notes new feature this month
React Native new architecture release performance change
SwiftUI new API WWDC iOS release agent skill
Jetpack Compose adaptive layout new release Android
App Store Review guideline change TestFlight Google Play policy update

tests.prompt: Start a habit-tracker app for iPhone and Android. Users add habits, check them off daily, see a streak. I don't have a stack yet. Plan it and build the first screens.
tests.good: Picks Expo + Expo Router with a one-line reason; maps navigation (tabs, push for detail, modal or sheet for add habit) before code; native controls, one accent, system colours, no emoji chrome; loading/empty/error states including a real empty state; FlashList or FlatList; checks light/dark and large text on simulator and emulator; says what still needs a real device.

tests.prompt: Xcode 26 now gives me 'Sending value of non-Sendable type risks causing data races' in my view model that loads photos. Here's the class. How do I fix it properly?
tests.good: Reads the build settings first (Swift 6 mode, default MainActor isolation, approachable concurrency); explains which isolation domains the value crosses; prefers keeping the work on the MainActor or making the type Sendable/a value type over @unchecked Sendable or nonisolated(unsafe); uses @concurrent only for measured heavy work; shows the fixed code and how to verify with the compiler.

tests.prompt: My Expo app is ready. Get it on TestFlight for my two co-founders today.
tests.good: Checks eas.json, app.json identifiers and Apple account state first; asks the user to run credential prompts themselves; uses eas build -p ios --profile production with auto-submit or npx testflight; adds internal testers (no review needed); reports the build ID and the furthest verified state (uploaded/processed/available to testers), not 'it's live'; does not submit for App Review.

tests.prompt: Build an Expo app for members of a small climbing gym: sign in, book a class, see and cancel their bookings. Keep the data in Supabase, and design an app icon we can use for the store listings.
tests.good: States a short plan first: the app here (native-feel-design.md, expo-react-native.md, testing-simulators.md), data and sign-in through backend-databases (supabase.md and postgres-schema.md: classes and bookings tables with RLS on every table, only the publishable key in the app, the service_role key never shipped; auth.md for sessions), the icon through poster-design (logos.md: one simple mark that still reads at 16 px; web-assets.md for the icon sizes). Maps navigation before code (tabs, push to class detail, sheet to book); builds loading, empty and error states; checks both themes and large text on simulator and emulator; checks the Done means of all three crafts.

tests.prompt: I have an Expo app (SDK 54, Expo Router, EAS Build already set up) and I need crash reporting and push notifications before launch. Add Firebase Crashlytics and Firebase Cloud Messaging for iOS and Android, make sure crashes show up readable with symbols, and tell me how to confirm it works end to end. I haven't created the Firebase project yet.
tests.good: Moves the app off Expo Go onto a development build and says why (@react-native-firebase needs native code); uses the @react-native-firebase/app and crashlytics config plugins in app config and React Native Firebase on RN 0.75+/Expo SDK 54 resolves Firebase through Swift Package Manager by default, which needs expo-build-properties ios.useFrameworks set to "dynamic"; static frameworks need disableSPM: true on the @react-native-firebase/app plugin plus useFrameworks "static" and forceStaticLinking, and must not be combined with default SPM, with GoogleService-Info.plist and google-services.json wired through app config and a note that API keys in them are identifiers while service-account keys and App Store Connect/APNs keys must never enter the repo. Covers FCM specifics: iOS needs an APNs auth key uploaded to Firebase, Android 13 notification permission prompt, and testing a token from a real device (not the simulator for FCM tokens). Explains symbolication: dSYM upload for iOS release builds, R8 mapping file for Android. Verifies with a deliberate test crash on a release or non-debugger build, then checks it in the Firebase console or via the Firebase MCP, and says what could not be verified without a real device. Asks before creating the Firebase project, running paid EAS builds or sending production pushes, and adds a consent/privacy mention for crash and analytics collection in the store privacy forms.

tools.name: Xcode
tools.why: The only way to build, sign, profile and upload native iOS/macOS apps; Xcode 26.3 (Feb 2026) added agentic coding with Claude Agent and a built-in MCP bridge (`xcrun mcpbridge`, 20 tools) per Apple's newsroom and InfoQ.

tools.name: Android Studio
tools.why: Google's official IDE and the standard for native Android (Gradle, emulator, profilers, APK analyzer; Gemini built in); named as the Android standard in 2026 round-ups such as spaceotechnologies and catdoes lists.

tools.name: React Native
tools.why: About 35% of cross-platform developers and about 13% of professional developers in Stack Overflow data; the majority choice among North American agencies (Statista-derived summaries).

tools.name: Expo & EAS
tools.why: The default way to start a React Native app; Expo ships official skills (2,655 stars), a remote MCP server on the Free plan, and EAS Build/Submit/Update used for most RN store releases (Expo docs and changelog).

tools.name: Flutter
tools.why: Used by about 46% of cross-platform developers in Statista-based 2026 round-ups and 9.1% of all developers in Stack Overflow 2025; Google ships official skills and a Dart/Flutter MCP server.

tools.name: SwiftUI
tools.why: Apple's primary UI framework for new iOS/macOS apps; three separate SwiftUI agent skills each have 3,600 to 5,000 stars, the strongest community signal in this craft.

tools.name: App Store Connect & TestFlight
tools.why: The only route to ship iOS apps; the App Store Connect API is Apple's official automation surface and TestFlight is the standard beta channel (Apple docs); asc CLI skills repo has 1,052 stars.

tools.name: Google Play Console
tools.why: The only route to publish on Google Play; the Play Developer API automates uploads, tracks, rollouts and subscriptions (Google docs). Official skills exist for Play Billing and policy insights.

tools.name: Firebase
tools.why: Named as the essential mobile backend/support stack (Crashlytics, FCM push, Auth, Remote Config, Analytics) in 2026 round-ups; Google ships an official MCP server and agent skills including Crashlytics.

tools.name: Jetpack Compose
tools.why: Primary UI toolkit for more than 78% of professional Android developers (2025 State of Android Developer survey) and used by 60% of the top 1,000 Play apps since Google I/O 2025; Android's recommended UI toolkit.

tools.name: Maestro
tools.why: Leading YAML E2E framework for iOS, Android, RN and Flutter (15.9k GitHub stars) with an official MCP server (`maestro mcp`) that lets an agent inspect screens and run flows.

tools.name: fastlane
tools.why: Long-standing Ruby automation for signing (match), TestFlight (pilot), metadata (deliver) and Play uploads (supply), still common in native and Flutter CI; no longer the only option now that asc and EAS exist.

tools.name: RevenueCat
tools.why: The common in-app purchase and subscription layer across iOS, Android, RN and Flutter; ships an official remote MCP server and an AI toolkit repo (73 stars).

tools.name: Sentry
tools.why: Widely used crash and performance monitoring for RN, Flutter and native (source maps, dSYM and R8 mapping upload); official MCP server and a 268-star skills repo with per-platform SDK setup skills.

tools.name: XcodeBuildMCP
tools.why: The most used MCP server and CLI for building, running, testing and UI-driving iOS/macOS apps from an agent (6,458 stars, now under getsentry, renamed MobileBuildMCP); an alternative to Xcode's own mcpbridge.

tools.name: Electron
tools.why: The most-used cross-platform desktop framework in 2026 (VS Code, Slack, Discord, Figma, Notion; about 1.6M+ weekly npm downloads versus Tauri's ~85k per 2026 comparisons); the router covers desktop apps but only Tauri and SwiftPM Mac apps.

tools.name: Kotlin Multiplatform
tools.why: Google-endorsed shared-code route for Android and iOS; usage among professional developers rose from about 7% to 18-23% in 2025-26 round-ups citing JetBrains surveys, with production use at Google Docs iOS, Duolingo, Netflix and Cash App.

tools.name: Xcode Cloud
tools.why: Apple's built-in CI/CD; the most used CI among iOS developers with pipelines in a June 2026 survey of 404 developers (34%, ahead of GitHub Actions 31% and fastlane 21%); builds, tests and delivers to TestFlight with an App Store Connect API for automation.

tools.name: Capacitor
tools.why: The standard way to ship an existing web app or PWA as an iOS/Android store app (successor to Cordova); Ionic and Cordova were each used by about 9-10% of cross-platform developers in Statista's 2023 survey; fills the gap between the PWA guide and the store-release guide.
